name: LM5007MMX_NOPB
title: 75 V, 0.5 A step-down converter with integrated 80 V N-channel switch
summary: The LM5007 is a buck regulator for inputs from 9 V to 75 V with an on-chip 80 V, 0.7 A N-channel high-side switch, delivering up to 0.5 A. Control is constant on-time: an external resistor from VIN to RON sets an on-time that falls as VIN rises, which holds the switching frequency nearly steady, and no loop compensation is needed. A cycle-by-cycle current limit is followed by an off-time that scales with the FB voltage and a resistor on RCL. It has a 7 V internal bias regulator, VCC and gate-drive UVLO, thermal shutdown, and a shutdown input on RON; it comes in 8-pin VSSOP and 8-pin WSON with exposed pad.

pins.name: SW
pins.function: Switch node: source of the internal buck switch. The output inductor and the cathode of the freewheeling diode connect to it.

pins.name: BST
pins.function: Bootstrap supply for the high-side gate driver. A capacitor goes from BST to SW, 0.01 µF ceramic recommended; an internal diode from VCC charges it.

pins.name: RCL
pins.function: Current-limit off-time setting. A resistor from RCL to RTN, together with the FB voltage, sets the off-time after a current-limit event: 17 µs with FB at 0 V, shorter as FB rises. tOFF = 10^-5 / (0.59 + VFB / (7.22 × 10^-6 × RCL)).

pins.name: FB
pins.function: Feedback input to the regulation comparator (its inverting side); the output regulates where FB sits at 2.5 V.

pins.name: RON
pins.function: On-time setting and shutdown. A resistor from VIN to RON sets the on-time, tON = 1.42 × 10^-10 × RON / VIN; at the highest input voltage the recommended minimum on-time is 300 ns. Pulling RON below 0.7 V shuts the converter down.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Output of the internal high-voltage bias regulator, 7 V nominal, current-limited to 10 mA; it powers the gate drive. A 0.1 µF local decoupling capacitor is recommended. Driving VCC from an auxiliary source above 7 V turns the internal regulator off and lowers dissipation; VCC must stay at or below 14 V. An internal diode runs from VCC to BST.

circuits.title: 12 V to 75 V input, 10 V 400 mA output buck converter
circuits.description: A complete step-down design worked through in the design procedure. RON (200 kΩ) from VIN sets the on-time for about 380 kHz; RFB2 and RFB1 (3.01 kΩ over 1 kΩ) divide the 10 V output down to the 2.5 V FB threshold. L1 (100 µH) and D1 form the power stage; RC (1 Ω) in series with COUT (15 µF) adds ESR-like ripple in phase with the inductor current so the comparator switches cleanly (ripple type 1). CBST bootstraps the gate drive, CVCC decouples the bias regulator, RCL (100 kΩ) sets the current-limit off-time, CIN and CBYP filter the input, and pulling the RON node low through the shutdown point stops the converter.

parts.note: ultra-fast or Schottky freewheeling diode rated above the highest input voltage
X5R or X7R, 16 V or higher

circuits.title: Low output ripple voltage configuration
circuits.description: The feedback divider R1 and R2 and a series resistor R take their signal at the inductor, ahead of the output capacitor, so FB sees the ripple of the inductor current flowing in R while the load connects directly to the low-ESR COUT. The ripple at the load stays small; R costs some load regulation.

circuits.title: Self-biased configuration, VOUT feeding VCC through a diode
circuits.description: A 10 V output feeds VCC through a self-bias diode. With VCC held above its 7 V set point the internal series regulator turns off and the IC dissipates less. The divider of 30 kΩ over 10 kΩ sets the output; 0.1 µF decouples VCC and 0.01 µF is the bootstrap capacitor.

circuits.title: Shutdown implementation
circuits.description: A switch from the RON node to ground stops the converter: in the STOP position it pulls RON below the 0.7 V threshold, which holds the buck switch off and disables the VCC regulator; in RUN the switch is open and RON sets the on-time normally.

circuits.title: Ripple network type 1, lowest cost
circuits.description: RC in series with COUT puts a resistive ripple in phase with the inductor current onto the output, and the divider RFB2 over RFB1 passes it to FB. RC is chosen for at least 25 mV at FB (equation for RC, type 1).

circuits.title: Ripple network type 2, reduced ripple
circuits.description: As type 1, with Cac across RFB2 so the output ripple reaches FB without the divider's attenuation; RC can then be smaller for the same 25 mV at FB, and the output ripple is lower.

circuits.title: Ripple network type 3, minimum ripple
circuits.description: Rr and Cr in series across the inductor integrate the switch-node voltage into a triangular ramp, and Cac couples that ramp into FB. The output ripple plays no part, so COUT can have very low ESR. Cr = 3.3 nF and Cac = 100 nF, with Rr from the type 3 equation.

where.R1: upper feedback resistor, VOUT to FB
where.R2: lower feedback resistor, FB to ground

where.RFB1 ∥ RFB2: parallel value of the feedback resistors

equations.name: Type 3 ripple network

operation.text: When FB is under the 2.5 V reference the switch turns on for one on-time, set by RON and VIN. It then stays off for at least 300 ns, and turns on again as soon as FB is back below the reference. At light load the inductor current falls to zero each cycle (DCM) and the frequency drops with load, which keeps light-load losses down; at heavier load conduction is continuous (CCM) and the frequency is nearly constant over line and load.

The comparator needs an output ripple in phase with the inductor current, so the output capacitor needs some ESR; 25 mV to 50 mV of ripple at FB is recommended. Where the capacitor's ESR is too low, a resistor can be added in series. A capacitor across the upper feedback resistor raises the ripple reaching FB. For stable switching the FB voltage must fall steadily, in phase with the inductor current, through the off-time, and that fall must be larger than noise on the node; at the output the ESR part of the ripple must outweigh the capacitive part, or the converter fires bursts of on-times followed by long off-times.

An internal regulator runs from VIN (9 V to 75 V) and supplies VCC, current-limited to 10 mA. At power-up it charges the VCC capacitor and the converter starts once VCC reaches 7 V. A ceramic capacitor of about 0.1 µF from VIN to RTN, close to the pins, guards against transients from lead inductance. An auxiliary supply above 7 V on VCC switches the internal regulator essentially off.
A second comparator watches FB against 2.875 V (VOV-REF) and ends the on-time at once if FB rises above it, protecting the output against sudden line or load steps.

RON is a low-impedance input held near 1.5 V, so the current in the resistor from VIN tracks VIN and sets an on-time inversely proportional to it, keeping the frequency nearly constant. Pulling RON below 0.7 V puts the part in a low-power shutdown: the switch is held off, the VCC regulator is disabled and the VIN current is about 100 µA inside the IC, with the RON resistor's own current on top.

If the switch current exceeds 725 mA the on-time ends in that cycle and an off-timer starts that cannot be cut short. Its length depends on RCL and on FB: 17 µs with FB at 0 V (a short), shorter as the output voltage rises under a lesser overload, which reduces foldback and shortens start-up. The current-limit off-time should be less than the normal steady-state off-time. With low-resistance inductors or low-drop diodes, a short at high input may need checking, since 17 µs may not balance the inductor volt-seconds; more inductor or output resistance, or a diode with a larger drop, may be needed. Useful RCL values are about 100 kΩ to 1 MΩ.

The N-channel buck switch has a floating gate driver powered from the bootstrap capacitor, which VCC charges through an internal high-voltage diode while SW is low. The 300 ns minimum off-time guarantees a recharge interval every cycle. A 0.01 µF ceramic BST-to-SW capacitor is recommended. An external diode from SW to RTN carries the inductor current while the switch is off; it must be ultra-fast or Schottky, and its reverse rating must exceed the highest input voltage.
At about 165 °C junction temperature the converter enters a low-power reset with the driver off. The threshold has 25 °C of hysteresis and the part recovers automatically.

At least 1 mA of load is needed. Below that the bootstrap capacitor can run down over long off-times, and the converter stops or cycles on and off slowly; the feedback divider can be made low enough in value to draw the minimum itself.
The part is meant for inputs above 9 V. The lowest working input is set by the VCC UVLO threshold of 6.3 V typ; if VIN cannot hold VCC above it the converter sits in standby with the switch off.

operation.topic: Output above the VCC set point
operation.text: With an output higher than the VCC regulation level, a diode from VOUT to VCC lets the output power the bias, for better efficiency and less heat in the IC.

The source must stay within the ratings and deliver the full-load input current. Long input leads form an underdamped resonance with low-ESR ceramic input capacitors, giving overshoot when power is applied and dips on load steps that can trip UVLO near the minimum input. Shorter leads and an aluminium or tantalum capacitor of 10 µF to 47 µF beside the ceramics damp it. A poorly designed EMI input filter can cause instability.

The comparators are fast and react to short noise spikes. Keep the loop of VIN pin, SW pin, freewheeling diode and input ceramic capacitor as small as possible: input capacitor close to VIN, diode cathode at SW and its anode by the input capacitor's return, and a short, wide copper connection to RTN under the IC. Put the inductor close to SW and keep the SW copper area small. Place CBST, RCL, RON and CVCC tight to their pins and both feedback resistors close to FB, and route the output sense trace away from the inductor. Use a solid ground plane on layer 2. For heat, solder the WSON exposed pad to a ground plane that extends beyond the package, use wide power traces and make use of airflow.
